question:
Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank.

Wedding is an auspicious _______ for all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. occasion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "occasion", meaning a particular time or event / a special or important event. (अवसर)

◦ Correct: Wedding is an auspicious occasion for all.

• Spelling key: OC + CA + SION (one "c" is doubled, single "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other options are misspelt — "occassion" (extra "s"), "occation" (wrong "t") and "ocassion" (single "c") are all wrong.

NOTE

• Remember: occasion has double "c" and single "s". Related word: "occasional" (happening from time to time), "occasionally".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Commence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Start.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Commence" means to begin or start something. Its closest synonym is "Start". (आरंभ करना / शुरू करना)

◦ Example: The examination will commence/start at 10 a.m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Subvert" (to undermine/overthrow), Option 2 "Exert" (to apply effort/force) and Option 4 "Escort" (to accompany) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of commence: start, begin, initiate, launch, embark on. Antonyms: end, conclude, finish, terminate, cease.

question:
In the given sentence, one of the four underlined words is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

She dabbled in drawing and painting, but scalpture was her favourite medium.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. scalpture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Scalpture" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "sculpture", meaning the art of making solid figures/objects by carving or modelling, or such a figure itself. (मूर्तिकला)

◦ Correct: ... but sculpture was her favourite medium.

• Spelling key: SCULP + TURE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "drawing", "favourite" (British spelling) and "dabbled" are all correctly spelt.

• "Dabbled" means to take part in an activity in a casual, not serious way.

NOTE

• Related words: sculptor (a person who makes sculptures), sculpt (verb — to carve/shape). Do not confuse with "scalp" (skin of the head).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I couldn't believe how _______ the math problem was; it took me hours to solve it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. complicated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause "it took me hours to solve it" shows the problem was difficult. So the adjective "complicated" (difficult, involving many confusing parts) correctly fills the blank. (जटिल / पेचीदा)

◦ Correct: I couldn't believe how complicated the math problem was; it took me hours to solve it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "good" does not match the idea of difficulty.

• Options 3 "simply" and 4 "easily" are adverbs and also give the opposite (easy) meaning; the blank needs an adjective after "how" describing the noun "problem".

NOTE

• After "how + ___ + the noun was", an adjective (complicated), not an adverb (simply/easily), is required. Synonyms of complicated: complex, intricate, difficult.

question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Sarah and Fidha entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_1: Sarah and Fidha are entering into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_2: Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_3: Sarah and Fidha had entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
option_4: Sarah and Fidha were entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The simple future tense is formed with "will + base form (V1) of the verb". The base form of "entered" is "enter", so the future form is "will enter".

◦ Correct: Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "are entering" is present continuous.

• Option 3 "had entered" is past perfect.

• Option 4 "were entered" is a wrong past passive form.

NOTE

• Simple future = will/shall + V1 (will enter, will go, will write). It expresses an action that will happen later.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

When Mr. Bhanot was told a few years back that he needed to lose _____ or face health problems, he transformed his life with the _________ of a personal trainer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. weight; help.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The context is about health problems and a personal trainer, so one needs to lose "weight" and does so with the "help" of a personal trainer. (वज़न; मदद)

◦ Correct: ... he needed to lose weight or face health problems, he transformed his life with the help of a personal trainer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "wait" is a homophone of "weight" but wrong in meaning here (to wait = to stay).

• Options 2 ("money; instructions") and 4 ("patience; guidance") do not fit the health/fitness context.

NOTE

• Homophones to distinguish: weight (heaviness) vs wait (to stay/pause). Both sound alike but differ in spelling and meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Confession is good for the soul ________________ after the soul has been claimed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. even.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverb "even" is used to emphasise something surprising or extreme. Here it stresses that confession benefits the soul "even after the soul has been claimed" (i.e., in the most extreme case). (यहाँ तक कि)

◦ Correct: Confession is good for the soul even after the soul has been claimed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "since" (because / from a time) and Option 2 "though" (although) change the logical relationship wrongly.

• Option 3 "still" would need a different sentence structure and does not give the emphatic sense required here.

NOTE

• "Even" adds emphasis: "even after", "even though", "even if". It highlights the unexpected or extreme nature of what follows.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She was a ________, ________ __________astronaut.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. smart, tall, Indian.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When several adjectives come before a noun, they follow a fixed order of adjectives: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Colour → Origin → Material → Purpose.

◦ Here "smart" (opinion) comes first, "tall" (size) next, and "Indian" (origin) last, just before the noun "astronaut".

◦ Correct: She was a smart, tall, Indian astronaut.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• The other options place the adjectives in the wrong sequence (e.g., origin before size), which sounds unnatural in English.

NOTE

• A common mnemonic for adjective order is OSASCOMP (Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Colour, Origin, Material, Purpose). Origin adjectives (Indian, French) always sit closest to the noun.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Callous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tender.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Callous" means insensitive, unfeeling and cruel; showing no concern for others. Its antonym is "Tender", meaning gentle, kind and caring. (कठोर / निर्दयी का विलोम — कोमल)

◦ Example: A callous remark hurt her, but his tender words comforted her.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Augment" (to increase), Option 2 "Desolate" (deserted/lonely — actually similar in gloom) and Option 4 "Beguile" (to charm or deceive) are not antonyms of callous.

NOTE

• Synonyms of callous: hard-hearted, insensitive, heartless, unfeeling. Antonyms: tender, kind, compassionate, sympathetic, caring.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the given word.

Species
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Type.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Species" means a class or kind/group of living things having common characteristics. Its closest synonym is "Type" (a kind, sort or category). (प्रजाति / प्रकार)

◦ Example: The zoo protects many species/types of endangered animals.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Whole" (entire/complete), Option 3 "Detail" (a small part/particular) and Option 4 "Multiply" (to increase in number) do not mean a kind or category.

NOTE

• Synonyms of species: type, kind, sort, class, category, variety. In biology, a species is a group of organisms that can interbreed.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Tranquil
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Unquiet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tranquil" means calm, peaceful and quiet. Its antonym is "Unquiet", meaning restless, disturbed and not calm. (शांत का विलोम — अशांत)

◦ Example: The lake was tranquil at dawn but grew unquiet during the storm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Composed" and 2 "Serene" are synonyms of tranquil (calm, peaceful).

• Option 3 "Shabby" (worn out/untidy) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of tranquil: calm, peaceful, serene, composed, placid, still. Antonyms: unquiet, restless, disturbed, agitated, turbulent.

question:
Identify the word with a spelling error in the following sentence. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

In Shakespeare's play 'Hamlet', Hamlet's flaw is defined as procrustineition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. procrastination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The misspelt word "procrustineition" should be corrected to "procrastination", meaning the act of delaying or postponing something / putting off tasks. (टाल-मटोल / विलंब करना)

◦ Correct: ... Hamlet's flaw is defined as procrastination.

• Spelling key: PRO + CRAS + TI + NA + TION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The other options — "pracrostination", "procristineition" and "procrustination" — are all incorrect spellings.

NOTE

• Related words: procrastinate (verb — to delay), procrastinator (a person who delays). Famous saying: "Procrastination is the thief of time."

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Mary is the quieter student of the class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. quietest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "of the class" implies a comparison among all the students of the class, which requires the superlative degree. The superlative of "quiet" is "quietest".

◦ Correct: Mary is the quietest student of the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "quieter" (comparative) is wrong because it compares only two things, whereas the whole class (a group) needs the superlative.

• "most quiet" and "more quiet" are wrong because a short adjective like "quiet" forms degrees with "-er/-est", not "more/most".

NOTE

• Degrees of "quiet": quiet – quieter (comparative, between two) – quietest (superlative, among many). Use "the + superlative" when comparing more than two.

question: Select the sentence with the most appropriate comparative degree.
option_1: She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra.
option_2: She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra.
option_3: She is more talented musician in the orchestra.
option_4: She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Talented" is a long adjective, so its superlative is formed with "the most". Comparing one musician with all others "in the orchestra" needs the superlative degree — "the most talented".

◦ Correct: She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses the noun "talent" wrongly ("the talent of all musicians").

• Option 2 "talentedest" is a wrong form (long adjectives never take "-est").

• Option 3 "more talented" is a comparative but omits "the" and does not fit comparison with the whole group.

NOTE

• Long adjectives: comparative = "more + adjective" (more talented), superlative = "the most + adjective" (the most talented). Short adjectives take "-er/-est".

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. old much.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct structure is "too + adjective + to + verb". So it should be "too old to join", not "old much to join". The segment "old much" is grammatically wrong.

◦ Correct: Ms. Malathi is too old to join a college now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• The segments "Ms. Malathi is", "to join" and "a college now" are all correct.

NOTE

• "Too ... to" shows an excessive degree that prevents an action (too old to join = so old that she cannot join). "Much" is used with comparatives (much older), not directly before an adjective like this.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Let the cat out of the bag
option_1: To buy a cat and a bag
option_3: To not allow a cat into the bag
option_4: To release a cat out of a bag
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. To reveal a secret.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "let the cat out of the bag" means to reveal a secret carelessly or by mistake. (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Example: She let the cat out of the bag and told everyone about the surprise party.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 3 and 4 give the literal (word-for-word) meaning, which is not what an idiom conveys. An idiom carries a figurative meaning.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about secrets: "spill the beans" (to reveal a secret), "give the game away", "blow the whistle" (to expose wrongdoing).

question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, choose the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

You cannot _________________ before replicating your successes and achievements multiple times; otherwise, people will deem your success a stroke of dumb luck.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. rest on your laurels.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "rest on your laurels" means to be so satisfied with past success that you stop making further effort. The sentence warns against relaxing after a single success. (पुरानी सफलताओं पर संतुष्ट होकर बैठ जाना)

◦ Correct: You cannot rest on your laurels before replicating your successes ... multiple times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "play devil's advocate" (to argue the opposite side for the sake of debate), Option 2 "sit on the fence" (to remain undecided) and Option 3 "cut to the chase" (to come to the point) do not fit the context.

NOTE

• "Laurels" refers to the laurel wreath awarded to winners in ancient times, symbolising honour/achievement. "Rest on one's laurels" = to become complacent after success.

question:
Select the correct indefinite article to fill in the blank.

My neighbour is ______ passionate photographer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The indefinite article "a" is used before words beginning with a consonant sound. "Passionate" begins with the consonant sound /p/, so "a passionate photographer" is correct.

◦ Correct: My neighbour is a passionate photographer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "an" is used before a vowel sound (an apple, an hour), which does not apply here.

• Option 4 "the" is a definite article (a specific one), not suitable for introducing a general description.

• Option 1 "one" is a number, not an article.

NOTE

• Rule of articles: "a" before a consonant sound (a boy, a university /yu/), "an" before a vowel sound (an egg, an honest man /o/). It depends on sound, not spelling.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the bracketed word in the sentence given below.

Surrounded by lush greenery, the house stood _____________ (submissively) atop a hill.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Proudly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Submissively" means in a meek, humble and obedient manner (yielding to others). Its antonym is "Proudly", meaning with dignity, self-respect and confidence. (विनम्रता/दब्बूपन से का विलोम — गर्व से)

◦ Example: The soldier stood proudly, not submissively, before the crowd.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Silently" (without noise), Option 2 "Civilly" (politely) and Option 3 "Magically" (as if by magic) are not opposites of submissively.

NOTE

• Synonyms of submissive: meek, obedient, yielding, docile, humble. Antonyms: proud, assertive, defiant, rebellious, dominant.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Shebna decided to take a break in social media, but she found it difficult to disconnect completely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. a break from social media.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "a break from (something)", meaning a period of rest or withdrawal away from it. So it should be "a break from social media".

◦ Correct: Shebna decided to take a break from social media ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "a break of", "a break up" and "a break down" are not the right prepositional phrases here.

• Note: "breakup" (end of a relationship) and "breakdown" (a failure/collapse) are different nouns with different meanings.

NOTE

• Preposition collocations: "take a break from work/study", "a break in the weather" (a pause), "break up with someone" (end a relationship).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. just.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs an adjective parallel to "equitable" to describe "society". "Just" (fair, based on justice) fits perfectly — "an equitable and just society". (न्यायपूर्ण / निष्पक्ष)

◦ Correct: ... developing an equitable and just society ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "much", Option 3 "such" and Option 4 "more" are not adjectives that can describe "society" in parallel with "equitable"; they are determiners/quantifiers and do not fit grammatically.

NOTE

• "Equitable" (fair and impartial) and "just" (right and fair) are close in meaning, used together to stress fairness. Both are adjectives modifying "society".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. access to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "access to (something)", meaning the opportunity or right to use/reach it. So it is "universal access to quality education".

◦ Correct: Providing universal access to quality education is the key ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "access at", "access from" and "access for" are incorrect prepositional combinations. The noun/verb "access" is always followed by "to".

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: "access to information / education / the internet". Example: "Everyone should have access to clean water."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. forward.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "the best way forward" is a common expression meaning the best course of action / the best method to make progress. It fits perfectly here. (आगे बढ़ने का सर्वोत्तम रास्ता)

◦ Correct: Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "outcome", 2 "output" and 3 "result" are nouns and would not fit the fixed phrase "the best way ___ for developing"; only "forward" makes it idiomatic.

NOTE

• "Way forward" = a plan or method for making progress. Example: "Dialogue is the only way forward in this dispute."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrase is "for the good of (someone/something)", meaning for the benefit of. So it is "for the good of the individual, the society, the country and the world".

◦ Correct: ... for the good of the individual, the society, the country and the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "the good from", "the good at" and "the good for" are not the correct prepositional phrase. The set expression is "for the good of".

NOTE

• "For the good of" = for the benefit/welfare of. Example: "The new law was passed for the good of the people."

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India's continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. will have.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage refers to the future ("over the next decade"), so the simple future tense "will have" is correct. India will have the highest population of young people.

◦ Correct: India will have the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "were having" is past continuous (wrong tense).

• Option 3 "might had" is grammatically incorrect (a modal is never followed by "had"; it should be "might have").

• Option 4 "can has" is grammatically wrong ("can" is always followed by the base form — "can have").

NOTE

• After a modal verb (will, can, might, may), always use the base form: "will have", "can have", "might have". "Over the next decade" signals the future tense.

question: 0.25 g of an organic compound, on treatment with fuming nitric acid followed by AgNO3, gave 0.22 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine in the compound is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 37.45%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a problem of Carius method for estimating halogen (bromine) in an organic compound.

◦ Formula: % of Br = (Atomic mass of Br / Molar mass of AgBr) × (mass of AgBr / mass of compound) × 100.

◦ Atomic mass of Br = 80; Molar mass of AgBr = 108 + 80 = 188.

◦ % of Br = (80 / 188) × (0.22 / 0.25) × 100 ≈ 37.45%.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In the Carius method, the organic compound is heated with fuming nitric acid and silver nitrate (AgNO₃) in a sealed Carius tube; the halogen forms a silver halide (AgCl, AgBr, AgI) precipitate that is weighed.

NOTE

• Silver halide molar masses: AgCl = 143.5, AgBr = 188, AgI = 235. This method is used for the quantitative estimation of halogens in organic compounds.

question: Rani ki Vav is a UNESCO world heritage monument, situated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rani ki Vav" (the Queen's Stepwell) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located at Patan in Gujarat, on the banks of the Saraswati River. (रानी की वाव — गुजरात)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It was built in the 11th century by Queen Udayamati in memory of her husband King Bhimdev I of the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014 and features on the ₹100 currency note.

NOTE

• Other UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Gujarat: Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, the Historic City of Ahmedabad, and Dholavira (a Harappan site).

question: Bathukamma festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bathukamma" is a colourful floral festival celebrated predominantly by the women of Telangana (and some parts of Andhra Pradesh). (बतुकम्मा — तेलंगाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• It is celebrated during the Navaratri period (September–October) and honours the goddess Gauri (Maha Gauri).

• Women arrange seasonal flowers in concentric layers to form a "Bathukamma" and sing and dance around it.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Telangana include Bonalu (dedicated to Goddess Mahakali). Bathukamma marks the beauty of nature and the onset of the festive season.

question: What is the collection of Vedic hymns or 'mantras' called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Samhita.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Samhita" is the collection of Vedic hymns or 'mantras'. Each Veda has its Samhita — the core collection of hymns. (संहिता — वैदिक मंत्रों का संग्रह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Each Veda is traditionally divided into four parts: Samhita (hymns), Brahmana (rituals/explanations), Aranyaka (forest treatises) and Upanishad (philosophy).

• The four Vedas are Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda. The Rigveda is the oldest.

NOTE

• Shruti ("that which is heard") includes the Vedas; Smriti ("that which is remembered") includes texts like the Manusmriti, Puranas and epics.

question: Usha Barle, who won Padma Shri 2023, is popularly associated with which genre of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandwani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Usha Barle, a Padma Shri 2023 awardee, is a renowned exponent of "Pandwani", a traditional folk singing/storytelling art form of Chhattisgarh based on the Mahabharata. (पंडवानी — उषा बारले)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandwani narrates tales of the Pandavas; the singer performs with a tambura and expressive gestures. Teejan Bai is its most famous exponent.

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India.

NOTE

• Lavani is a folk form of Maharashtra; Panihari and Kajari are folk songs associated with Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh/Bihar respectively.

question: In which of the following years India hosted the Women's Asia Cup ODI Cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India hosted the Women's Asia Cup ODI Cricket in the year 2006. (महिला एशिया कप — 2006)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Indian women's cricket team has been the most dominant side in the Women's Asia Cup, winning the title multiple times.

• The Asia Cup is organised by the Asian Cricket Council (ACC).

NOTE

• India's women's cricket has produced stars like Mithali Raj, Jhulan Goswami, Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana.

question: Alarmel Valli was associated with which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alarmel Valli is a celebrated exponent of the Bharatanatyam classical dance form, known for the Pandanallur style. (भरतनाट्यम — अलार्मेल वल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• Alarmel Valli has been honoured with the Padma Bhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: When protein-rich gelatinous egg white is heated, it turns to solid white due to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protein Denaturation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When egg white is heated, its proteins (mainly albumin) unfold and change structure permanently — this is called "protein denaturation" — turning the clear gelatinous liquid into a solid white. (प्रोटीन विकृतीकरण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Denaturation is the loss of the natural (native) three-dimensional structure of a protein due to heat, acids, or other agents, though the peptide bonds are not broken.

• The change is usually irreversible (a boiled egg cannot become raw again).

NOTE

• Emulsification = mixing of two immiscible liquids (oil and water); Fermentation = breakdown by microbes; Gluten formation occurs in wheat dough — none of these explain the setting of egg white.

question: In which of the following states are the Nor Westers known as 'Bardoisila'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Assam, the violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms known as Nor'westers (Kalbaisakhi) are locally called "Bardoisila". (असम — बरदोईछिला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• In West Bengal, the same Nor'westers are called "Kalbaisakhi" (the calamity of the month of Baisakh).

• These storms bring heavy rain and strong winds and are beneficial for tea, jute and rice cultivation.

NOTE

• Pre-monsoon showers have local names: "Mango showers" (Kerala/Karnataka), "Blossom showers" (Karnataka coffee), "Kalbaisakhi" (West Bengal), "Bardoisila" (Assam).

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
A) Balshastri Jambhekar started the first Anglo-Maratha newspaper - 'Durpun', in 1832.
B) He is remembered as the father of Marathi journalism.
C) Balshastri Jambhekar published the first Marathi monthly magazine - 'Digdurshun' in 1840.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, B and C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three statements about Balshastri Jambhekar are correct:

◦ A) He started the first Anglo-Marathi newspaper "Durpun (Darpan)" in 1832.

◦ B) He is remembered as the "Father of Marathi Journalism".

◦ C) He published the first Marathi monthly magazine "Digdurshun (Digdarshan)" in 1840.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Balshastri Jambhekar (1812–1846) was a social reformer, journalist and educationist from Maharashtra.

• "Darpan" was a bilingual paper (Marathi and English) that promoted social reform and modern education.

NOTE

• The father of Indian journalism is often considered James Augustus Hicky, who started the "Bengal Gazette" (Hicky's Gazette) in 1780, India's first newspaper.

question: Identify the correct statement with reference to the Padma awards.
option_1: The Padma award can be used as a suffix or prefix to the awardees' name
option_2: The total number of Padma awards to be given in a year should not more than 150.
option_3: The Padma Awards are given annually.
option_4: The names of the awardees are never published in the Gazette of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Padma Awards are given annually.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Padma Awards are announced every year on Republic Day (26 January) — i.e., they are given annually. This is the correct statement. (पद्म पुरस्कार — प्रतिवर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards are of three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri (in decreasing order of importance).

• The awards should not be used as a prefix or suffix to the awardee's name (so option 1 is wrong).

• The total number given in a year is generally not more than 120 (excluding posthumous, NRI/foreigner cases), so option 2 (150) is wrong.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, followed by Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri. Padma awards are conferred by the President of India.

question: Which of the following is NOT a component of revenue receipt?
option_3: Fees paid for the registration of property
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amount borrowed from World Bank.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amount borrowed from the World Bank" is a capital receipt, NOT a revenue receipt, because borrowing creates a liability (it has to be repaid). (उधार ली गई राशि — पूँजीगत प्राप्ति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets — e.g., taxes (GST), fees, fines, grants. So GST, registration fees and grants from UNESCO are revenue receipts.

• Capital receipts either create a liability (borrowings) or reduce assets (disinvestment).

NOTE

• Government receipts = Revenue Receipts (tax + non-tax) + Capital Receipts (borrowings, recovery of loans, disinvestment). Borrowings always fall under capital receipts.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population growth rate in Kerala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.9%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, Kerala recorded a decadal (2001–2011) population growth rate of about 4.9% — the lowest among all the major states of India. (केरल — 4.9%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kerala's low growth rate is attributed to its high literacy, better healthcare, women's empowerment and effective family planning.

• India's overall decadal growth rate (2001–2011) was 17.7%.

NOTE

• Kerala also has the highest literacy rate and a favourable (high) sex ratio in India. The Census of India 2011 was the 15th National Census and was conducted under C. Chandramauli.

question: In April 2023, who was appointed as the chairman of the National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) by the centre?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arun Sinha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2023, Arun Sinha was appointed as the Chairman of the National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) by the central government. (अरुण सिन्हा — NTRO अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The NTRO is a technical intelligence agency under the National Security Adviser (NSA) in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).

• It was established in 2004 and works in areas such as satellite and terrestrial monitoring, cyber security and cryptology.

NOTE

• India's key intelligence agencies: RAW (external intelligence), IB (Intelligence Bureau) (internal), and NTRO (technical intelligence). The current NSA is Ajit Doval.

question: Which of the following is an example of the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Humayun's tomb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Humayun's Tomb" in Delhi is the first garden-tomb (charbagh-style tomb) on the Indian subcontinent. (हुमायूँ का मकबरा — पहला उद्यान-मकबरा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It was built in 1570 by Bega Begum (Haji Begum), the widow of Emperor Humayun, and designed by the Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993 and is said to have inspired the design of the Taj Mahal.

NOTE

• The "charbagh" is a four-part Persian-style garden divided by walkways or water channels. Humayun's Tomb was the first major Mughal building to use red sandstone on such a large scale.

question: According to the Census 2011, what was the annual population growth rate of India (in percentage)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.64%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census 2011, the annual (average) population growth rate of India was about 1.64%. (भारत की वार्षिक जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर — 1.64%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The decadal (10-year) growth rate for 2001–2011 was 17.7%, which corresponds to an average annual growth of roughly 1.64%.

• The Census 2011 recorded India's total population at about 121 crore (1.21 billion).

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every ten years; the first synchronous census was in 1881. The 2011 Census had the theme "Our Census, Our Future".

question: The Indian Forest Service was created under the All India Service Act, 1951 in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1966.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indian Forest Service (IFS) was constituted in 1966 under the All India Services Act, 1951. It is one of the three All India Services. (भारतीय वन सेवा — 1966)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The three All India Services are the IAS (Indian Administrative Service), IPS (Indian Police Service) and IFoS (Indian Forest Service).

• The IFS manages the country's forests, wildlife and environment; officers are trained at the Indira Gandhi National Forest Academy, Dehradun.

NOTE

• The IAS and IPS have their roots in the pre-independence Imperial services, while the IFS was created after independence in 1966. All India Services are governed by Article 312 of the Constitution.

question: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry is included in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 48.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 48 of the Constitution deals with the "Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry" on modern and scientific lines, and the preservation and improvement of breeds and prohibition of slaughter of cows and other cattle. (अनुच्छेद 48)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Article 48 is a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) under Part IV of the Constitution.

• Article 48A (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976) deals with the protection of the environment, forests and wildlife.

NOTE

• Other DPSPs: Article 45 (early childhood care/education), Article 46 (promotion of SCs/STs and weaker sections), Article 47 (raising the level of nutrition and public health).

question: In which of the following Indian states is the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "M.A. Chidambaram Stadium" (also known as Chepauk Stadium) is a famous cricket stadium located in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. (एम.ए. चिदंबरम स्टेडियम — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It is one of the oldest cricket stadiums in India and is the home ground of the Tamil Nadu cricket team and the IPL franchise Chennai Super Kings (CSK).

• It is managed by the Tamil Nadu Cricket Association (TNCA).

NOTE

• Other major cricket stadiums: Eden Gardens (Kolkata), Wankhede Stadium (Mumbai), M. Chinnaswamy Stadium (Bengaluru) and the Narendra Modi Stadium (Ahmedabad — the world's largest).

question: The famous English novel 'Em and the Big Hoom' is written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jerry Pinto.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous English novel "Em and the Big Hoom" was written by Jerry Pinto. (जेरी पिंटो)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The novel, published in 2012, deals with a family coping with a mother's mental illness (bipolar disorder) and won the Hindu Literary Prize and the Windham–Campbell Prize.

• Jerry Pinto is an Indian writer, poet and journalist based in Mumbai.

NOTE

• Notable books: Amitav Ghosh ("The Shadow Lines", "The Hungry Tide"), Shashi Tharoor ("The Great Indian Novel", "Why I Am a Hindu"), Esther David ("The Book of Rachel").

question: Which of the following is NOT an element of weather?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Plants.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plants" are NOT an element of weather. The main elements of weather are temperature, humidity, air pressure, wind, and rainfall/precipitation. (पौधे — मौसम का तत्व नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere at a place, while climate is the average weather over a long period (about 30 years).

• Weather is studied under meteorology.

NOTE

• Elements/components of weather and climate: temperature, atmospheric pressure, wind, humidity, cloudiness and precipitation. Plants are part of the biosphere, not the atmosphere.

question: Which of the following organisms is used in bread and alcohol industries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yeast.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Yeast" (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is a fungus used in the bread and alcohol (brewing) industries. It carries out fermentation, converting sugars into carbon dioxide and alcohol. (यीस्ट / खमीर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In bread-making, the CO₂ released by yeast makes the dough rise (leavening).

• In the alcohol industry, yeast ferments sugars to produce ethanol (as in beer and wine).

NOTE

• Clostridium and Nitrobacter are bacteria (Nitrobacter helps in nitrogen fixation/nitrification); Penicillium is a fungus used to make the antibiotic penicillin.

question: In Union Budget 2023-24, annual production of 5 MMT under Green Hydrogen Mission is to be targeted by the year ___________ to facilitate transition of the economy to low carbon intensity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2030.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Union Budget 2023-24, under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, an annual production of 5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes) of green hydrogen is targeted by the year 2030, to facilitate the economy's transition to low carbon intensity. (हरित हाइड्रोजन मिशन — 2030)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved in January 2023 with an outlay of about ₹19,700 crore.

• Green hydrogen is produced by the electrolysis of water using renewable energy, producing no carbon emissions.

NOTE

• India aims to become a global hub for green hydrogen production and export, supporting its goal of achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2070.

question: The Prime Minister in India is ________.
option_3: the Supreme Commander of Armed Forces
solution_text:
The correct answer is the real executive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the Prime Minister is the real executive (de facto head) who actually exercises executive power and runs the government. (प्रधानमंत्री — वास्तविक कार्यपालिका)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The President is the nominal/constitutional head (de jure) and also the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.

• The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.

NOTE

• Article 74 provides that the President acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The Chief Justice of India heads the judiciary, not the PM.

question: According to the Census of India-2011, what is the share of workforce engaged in the agriculture sector?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 54.6%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, about 54.6% of the total workforce was engaged in the agriculture sector (as cultivators and agricultural labourers). (कृषि क्षेत्र में कार्यबल — 54.6%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• This shows that a majority of Indians still depend on agriculture and allied activities for their livelihood, even though its share in GDP is much smaller (around 15–18%).

• The workforce is classified as main workers, marginal workers and non-workers in the Census.

NOTE

• Agriculture is the primary sector of the economy. India's large agricultural workforce reflects disguised unemployment in rural areas.
